problem: B1 certifies later bytes than semantic checks read; a cached true attempt can survive a real external attempt change. B2 sends all history rows in one65KiB result and thereby blocks every nonpoll action as legal history grows. Fix the snapshot/certificate boundary and history communication together without changing runtime semantics.
design_boundary: Preserve the single supervisor, current isolated helper groups/FD allowlist, nonblocking event loop and two authorized product files. Replace the helper result/files_checked mechanism and its unconditional check_live bypass. No new public call/schema, project lane, external package/service or arbitrary executable is introduced. Lisp capture/printing remains unchanged.
B1_exact_semantic_snapshot: Create a read-only snapshot view before semantic evaluation. Every attempt/session/controller/handoff/operation/result/source read used by validation must obtain bytes through that view. Open a regular input, record identity/stat before read, read/hash bytes, check the same identity/stat afterward, and retain the exact immutable bytes, digest and parsed value. Missing/extra directory entries, replacement, partial reads, malformed JSON or changed identity fail closed. Do not independently reopen later bytes and attach an earlier boolean to them.

Run attempt_matches semantics, complete history relations and source/template validation against this exact view. Source committed bytes, working bytes and requested manifest digests must agree within the same transaction; verify requested Git revision before and after source validation. Bind the decoded attempt/contract/step and live owner/generation/lease/outstanding record reference into the certificate, not only attempt_ok. Failed attempt comparison retains attempt_mismatch; inconsistent records retain ambiguous_state.

Establish filesystem-change monitoring before snapshot collection, covering authoritative record/run_state inputs, the operation directory and source/Git identity inputs used by the request, including replacement/rename and relevant ancestor changes. A Linux nonblocking change-monitor descriptor, accessed through Python standard-library ctypes and existing libc, can bridge helper validation to supervisor publication without parent file scans. Directory/name filtering must cover every certified input; inability to establish coverage, queue overflow, lost watch, unclassifiable event or inode/path disagreement invalidates the transaction.

After semantic checks, revalidate the snapshot bytes/digests and namespace inside the helper and drain its change epoch. Transfer the read-only change-monitor descriptor to the parent over the private Unix job channel, with a bounded certificate. Parent retains monitoring through helper-group cleanup and immediately before publication: drain notifications, require unchanged epoch and supervisor version, exact request/action/runtime/owner/generation/lease/outstanding/binding and currently certified decoded attempt. An external edit after semantic validation must invalidate admission even when self.version is unchanged.

Consume a certificate once for its exact request and state version. Never treat any non-null verification object as permission to skip check_live, and never allow a certificate for one operation/kind/source/attempt to authorize another. The publication linearization point is the final unchanged-epoch/identity check directly before the existing ordered durable transition and execute/cancel queueing. No blocking read, Git call or full-history scan occurs between that check and publication. Later changes invalidate subsequent transitions; no cross-process filesystem transaction or authentication guarantee is claimed.
B2_complete_history_scaling: Keep every historical operation/result and all generation/nonce, executed/status, cancellation/result and crash-disagreement relations. Establish the full validated history in an isolated helper, producing a content-addressed certificate over the entire namespace and exact validated record bytes, including count, root digest and generation relations. Do not serialize the complete path/stamp/hash table to the parent.

Retain this validated history view in private supervisor/helper state across the live generation. Extend it only with exact bytes of the supervisor own already-ordered publications and validation of each affected relation; preserve the complete validated prefix and digest rather than rescanning or retransmitting it for every call. The operation-directory change monitor distinguishes expected own publication events from unexpected mutations. Unexpected changes invalidate eligibility and require complete asynchronous reconciliation; no invalidation may be treated as an unchanged prefix.

Use a fixed-size result certificate for the history root/count, request digest, validated identity/binding and change epoch. Provenance values already present in the bounded parent request need only a digest and validation decision, not another unbounded copy. Any genuinely variable private payload must use correlated bounded chunks with sequence/count/digest and explicit credits, a bounded receive window and a terminal seal. Parent processes bounded chunks per turn and never accumulates a whole history response in a65KiB frame or silently truncates/omits rows.

Cancellation and close use the same complete validated history certificate plus exact current mutable records and live attempt, so untouched completed history adds no per-request response size or parent scan. This removes the deterministic history-size ceiling before cancellation publication/arming. Preserve duplicate-ID precedence against all existing IDs and detect orphan/extra records, missing results and old-generation inconsistencies; an incremental view is valid only while its complete monitored prefix remains certified.

When history becomes genuinely uncertain, preserve unknown/quarantine and refuse execution or a successful close/reconstruction claim until reconciliation resolves it. Continue servicing already armed cancellation and owned-group stop deadlines independently of that reconciliation. If stopping is required for an already proven owned runtime, observe its actual group boundary without certifying inconsistent history or fabricating cancelled/closed. Invalidate stale certificates rather than reuse them to bypass uncertainty. Resource/monitor/job failures remain truthful infrastructure failures; no file-count or transport-byte cutoff may masquerade as semantic history validation.
private_helper_and_monitor_lifetime: Retain the Source3 explicit descriptor closure before verification: helper only owns its private job channel, required start authorization/read-only inputs and deliberate standard streams; no supervisor flock/listener/client/runtime/protocol/parent/sibling descriptors. Any transferred monitor descriptor is newly created by that helper, read-only observation capability, never runtime control or publication authority; validate descriptor/message/job association and close it on every rejection or completed lifetime.

Helper result readiness does not bypass separately proven helper/Git-descendant group cleanup. Keep nonce/PID/start-token/PGID/SID/uid handshake, bounded job/TERM/KILL/death phases, stale/malformed/late/EOF rejection, bounded buffers and sole Supervisor publication. A transferred monitor remains owned by the supervisor after actual helper-group death, closing the old validation-to-cleanup race window. Unresolved helper ownership still blocks new admission/handoff/closed/reconstruction claims while runtime timers continue.

Monitor setup/drain and bounded private-channel processing must remain nonblocking and fairly batched; no whole-history parent read/stat loop, child wait, arbitrary callback or source/Git traversal enters deadline servicing. Overflow/coverage loss must conservatively invalidate certificates. Exact kernel event coverage and descriptor handoff require qualification after a separate Source4 release; this plan is not proof that those mechanisms work.

Keep conservative evaluate/partial-load/compile quarantine; all handler-bind pre-unwind active type/frame/restart evidence, bounded trusted rendering and existing omission markers.

tradeoffs: A constant-size certificate alone cannot prove currentness of history whose rows were omitted; monitoring and a retained fully validated view are the corresponding safety boundary. Incremental certification avoids repeated full-history transport/work for safety calls, while uncertain histories still require complete helper reconciliation. This adds a private Linux change-monitor mechanism but avoids public API/dependency changes or parent blocking scans. Missing reliable coverage is a blocking implementation issue, never permission to weaken the guards.
